Findings.Issue: Spot reserve manipulation enables mispriced synthetic issuance and redemption
Findings.Description: VaderPoolV2.mintSynth and burnSynth calculate synthetic conversion amounts directly from the current reserveNative and reserveForeign values using VaderMath.calculateSwap. These reserves can be changed by permissionless swaps through VaderRouterV2.swapExactTokensForTokens, which invokes BasePoolV2.swap and updates pairInfo reserves. Neither synthetic function uses a TWAP, external oracle, price-deviation bound, or user-supplied minimum-output parameter. An attacker can therefore move the pool price before a mint or redemption and cause synthetic assets to be issued or redeemed at a manipulated rate.
Findings.Impact: Users may receive materially fewer synth tokens or native assets than expected, while favorable manipulation can cause excessive synth issuance or native-asset redemption. Repeated exploitation may create mispriced synthetic liabilities, deplete pool reserves, and transfer value between users, liquidity providers, and attackers.
Findings.Location: contracts/dex-v2/pool/VaderPoolV2.sol — VaderPoolV2.mintSynth; contracts/dex-v2/pool/VaderPoolV2.sol — VaderPoolV2.burnSynth; contracts/dex-v2/pool/BasePoolV2.sol — BasePoolV2.swap
Findings.Mitigation: Price synth issuance and redemption using a sufficiently long and validated TWAP or an independent oracle rather than instantaneous reserves. Add user-controlled minimum-output parameters and deadlines, and reject execution when the pool price deviates beyond a configured threshold from the reference price. Review the reserve model so synth issuance and redemption cannot create inconsistent reserve-based pricing.

Findings.Issue: LiquidityBasedTWAP uses attacker-controlled spot reserves as historical weights
Findings.Description: LiquidityBasedTWAP derives pair liquidity weights from current spot reserves during syncVaderPrice and syncUSDVPrice. The values are stored as pastLiquidityEvaluation and later determine each pair's contribution to the aggregate VADER or USDV price. Because synchronization is publicly callable and the underlying reserves can be changed through swaps, an attacker can distort a pair's reserve composition immediately before synchronization, record manipulated weights, and later influence the aggregate oracle price even after reversing the trade. The synchronization logic also replaces the global total with only pairs that updated during the call, temporarily excluding pairs whose update period has not elapsed.
Findings.Impact: The aggregate oracle price used by USDV minting, USDV burning, and impermanent-loss reimbursement can be materially distorted. This may cause excess USDV issuance, excess VADER redemption or minting, and excessive reserve reimbursements. Incomplete pair inclusion can additionally produce unstable or malformed oracle outputs.
Findings.Location: contracts/lbt/LiquidityBasedTWAP.sol — LiquidityBasedTWAP.syncVaderPrice; contracts/lbt/LiquidityBasedTWAP.sol — LiquidityBasedTWAP.syncUSDVPrice; contracts/lbt/LiquidityBasedTWAP.sol — LiquidityBasedTWAP._updateVaderPrice; contracts/lbt/LiquidityBasedTWAP.sol — LiquidityBasedTWAP._updateUSDVPrice
Findings.Mitigation: Use time-weighted or otherwise historical liquidity measurements instead of spot reserves sampled at synchronization time. Recompute aggregate totals from all stored pair weights, retaining prior values for pairs that are not yet eligible for an update. Require nonzero totals, minimum pair liquidity, fresh observations, bounded per-update price changes, and independent reference-price deviation checks before accepting a new oracle value.

Findings.Issue: AMM-derived LBT prices can manipulate USDV conversion rates
Findings.Description: USDV.mint and USDV.burn consume prices returned by LiquidityBasedTWAP.getVaderPrice and getUSDVPrice. These prices are derived from cumulative prices of configured AMM pools and, for USDV pricing, VaderPoolV2 cumulative prices. An attacker can alter the underlying pool reserve ratio and maintain the manipulated state until the configured update period elapses, causing the LBT to record a distorted average price. The source permits any nonzero update period and does not enforce a minimum observation window, independent price validation, or maximum price deviation.
Findings.Impact: A manipulated VADER price can cause USDV.mint to issue excess USDV for deposited VADER. A manipulated USDV price can cause USDV.burn to mint excess VADER for burned USDV, potentially diluting VADER holders and increasing protocol liabilities. The lock delay does not correct an incorrectly calculated conversion amount.
Findings.Location: contracts/tokens/USDV.sol — USDV.mint; contracts/tokens/USDV.sol — USDV.burn; contracts/lbt/LiquidityBasedTWAP.sol — LiquidityBasedTWAP.getVaderPrice; contracts/lbt/LiquidityBasedTWAP.sol — LiquidityBasedTWAP.getUSDVPrice
Findings.Mitigation: Enforce a protocol-defined minimum TWAP update period and minimum liquidity threshold for configured pairs. Add independent oracle comparisons, maximum deviation and per-update movement limits, stale-data checks, and circuit breakers before accepting prices. USDV mint and burn operations should reject zero, stale, or abnormal prices and should support user-specified minimum-output protections.

Findings.Issue: Nominal swap inputs can corrupt price-bearing reserves for non-standard tokens
Findings.Description: VaderRouterV2 transfers the nominal amountIn to BasePoolV2 and passes the same nominal value to swap or doubleSwap. BasePoolV2.swap does not measure the actual balance increase before calculating output or updating reserves. If a supported token charges transfer fees, rebases, or otherwise transfers fewer tokens than requested, the pool calculates output and records reserves as though the full nominal amount was received. BasePoolV2.doubleSwap performs a balance sufficiency check but still uses the nominal input rather than the actual transfer delta.
Findings.Impact: The pool may pay output for tokens it did not receive and record overstated reserves. Subsequent swaps, liquidity withdrawals, cumulative prices, and oracle consumers can use corrupted reserve data, creating incorrect or manipulable prices and potentially causing direct pool losses or later transfer failures.
Findings.Location: contracts/dex-v2/pool/BasePoolV2.sol — BasePoolV2.swap; contracts/dex-v2/pool/BasePoolV2.sol — BasePoolV2.doubleSwap; contracts/dex-v2/router/VaderRouterV2.sol — VaderRouterV2._swap
Findings.Mitigation: Measure each token's actual balance increase relative to its stored reserve after the router transfer and use that value for swap calculations and reserve updates. Alternatively, explicitly reject any transfer where the received amount differs from the requested amount and restrict supported assets to standard ERC-20 tokens whose transfer behavior is compatible with nominal accounting. Apply the same validation to both legs of doubleSwap and update reserves from actual post-operation balances where practical.
